You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Compared with the source image, has the requested frog-in-the-toilet edit been made, and is it complete rather than only partial?
node.criteria: Pass if the edited image shows the requested frog placed inside the toilet bowl and the requested change is complete. Fail if the image clearly shows no progress toward placing a frog in the toilet, or shows progress but the requested change is clearly only partial. Do not infer incompleteness from extra frogs alone; judge whether the requested change itself is complete. Unknown if the source or edited image does not provide enough visual evidence to determine progress or completion.
node.binding: Compare the source and edited images, using the toilet in the source image as the reference. Inspect the frog's placement relative to the toilet bowl and the edited scene as a whole; account for visible frogs on the raised lid or floor without treating their presence alone as proof of failure.

node_traces.evidence: The source shows the toilet bowl without a frog. In the edited image, a frog is visibly placed inside the toilet bowl. Other frogs appear on the raised lid and floor, but the requested placement in the bowl is present and complete.

response.content: {"text":"The binding already identifies the bowl as the target, and the trace provides direct visual evidence of a frog inside it; extra frogs on the lid and floor do not by themselves establish incompleteness. The disagreement is therefore not explained by a missing placement check. The node’s criterion may be conflating “a frog is in the bowl” with “the requested edit is complete,” while the reference label only constrains the aggregate and does not say which visual detail makes this instance partial. Refine the decision procedure to assess progress and completion separately against the instruction, and require a specific, visible reason for calling the requested change partial rather than inferring it from unrelated additions. If the evidence cannot resolve that reason, preserve uncertainty instead of asserting a high-confidence yes. The trace is valid and queried with no dependency or transport failure, so investigate semantic criterion/routing and confidence calibration, not execution plumbing."}
